tasks.prompt:
SITUATION. Hackathon Live Final at 13:30, code freeze 13:00 - about 2 hours 20 minutes from now. The final plays HIDDEN cases (5 waves x 8 minutes, no human in the loop), drawn from the 46 profiled suppliers of the data package, possibly new case setups and structures. A case that ends in a walk-away, a timeout or a broken must-have scores 0 (or the alternative). Our agent averages 0.78 on the 10 hosted practice cases (top team 0.83). The four reports runs/night/out/fable_*.md summarise everything we learned from 225 practice sessions - read them first; their policy fixes 1-3 (c_track comparison, visible lead step, half-gap jump cap, close with the wider deadband alone) are already merged in policy.py. runs/cases/practice.json holds all 21 case files (only P01-P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18 are hosted for practice; P06, P09, P12-P17, P19 were never played), runs/cases/sandbox.json the sandbox cases.

We are going all in: we want changes that raise the score on unseen cases and remove every path to a zero. Each change must be implementable and testable in the next 90 minutes.

DELIVERABLE. Ranked findings, each with evidence (file:line, case id, numbers), the exact change as a minimal unified diff against the files shown (code files carry no comments), the cases it affects, the expected effect and the risk. At most 3,500 words.

YOUR QUESTION: Walk our policy (policy.py, costing.py, agent.py) mentally through EVERY one of the 21 case files, especially the 11 never played: negotiable fields, fixed_terms, term_options, must_haves, alternative, index_paths, multi-part bundles, tooling, incoterm, chargeback, lead time caps, volume options, RFQ bidders, effective dates. Find every place where we would send an incomplete or invalid sheet, break a must-have, pick a costly structure, mis-cost the alternative, crash on a missing key, walk away wrongly, or ignore a lever worth money (compute with cost.py). Give the fixes.

YOUR QUESTION: Claims are the one lever that lowers a supplier's first counter (see fable_round1.md). Compare the claim types the brief and api.md allow (and the claims suppliers made about us or themselves) with what claims.py builds and how pick_claims ranks them. Design the missing claim types that should lower first counters on hidden cases - e.g. a rebuttal that the supplier's price letter overshoots its own cost drivers' index-weighted change, should-cost gaps, negotiation-history settled-vs-asked, capacity/news, the alternative's offer, payment-history - with exact data sources in the package (package.py, profile.py), the sentence, the refs, and the check() branch so they verify. Give complete code.

Find every path to a timeout (60 s per move, 3 in a row end a thread), a crash, an unhandled exception, a hang, a lost accept, or a session left unplayed when 5 waves x several cases run in parallel; check the LLM calls have hard deadlines with template / rule fallbacks, that accept/final decisions never wait on an LLM, that a crashed case is restarted, and that rate limits (10 calls/s, 10 open sessions) hold. Give minimal fixes.
